What Woodlands Homes builds

Houses, bungalows, barn conversions and extensions, from the firm’s own gallery. Ask for a visit to see completed projects in person.

New homes

Unique homes of outstanding quality around Newark and Lincoln.

Woodlands Homes tries to use traditional natural materials, with as many modern comforts as possible: underfloor heating, air conditioning, heat recovery, rain savers, and solar, wind and ground heat source energy.

Clay stock bricks, clay or slate roof tiles, and corbelling on gables and eaves that matches the surrounding area. Self-builders are welcome: Woodlands Homes will show new clients around completed developments.

Barn conversions

Reclaimed bricks, clay pantiles and made-to-match joinery.

Sympathetic restoration of barns and listed buildings, working with local planners and conservation officers. Woodlands Homes makes replacement king post trusses, and tailors windows, doors, staircases and kitchens to the building.

It has also completed conversions under permitted development, from steel framed agricultural buildings to former offices.

Extensions, alterations and sun rooms

From a single trade to a full extension.

Woodlands Homes can provide the project drawings, deal with planning permission, and then supply individual trades: groundwork, brickwork, plastering, joinery, electrics and flooring.

A sun room differs from a conservatory because it is part of the home all year round: insulated walls and ceiling, a tiled roof, double glazed windows and doors, and the option of underfloor heating.

Conservation areas and listed buildings

Work that fits its surroundings.

Woodlands Homes works in conservation areas and on all types of listed building, alongside planners, building control officers and local authorities.

Traditional materials wherever possible: stock bricks, clay or slate roof tiles, purpose made wooden windows and doors, and cedar wood garage doors.

Kitchens and joinery

Fitted by the trades that know them.

Rigid carcasses with superb drawer boxes, quality appliances, granite worktops where needed, and a full ceramic tiling service for floors and walls. Joiners, plumbers, tilers and electricians fit each kitchen.

Dean has won awards for kitchen design, according to the Woodlands Homes website. Bespoke staircases and purpose made joinery are made to suit the character of the house.

How a job is run

  • A plan before the first brick

    Woodlands Homes works with architects, planners, conservation officers and building control, and with specialist craftsmen on site. It gives a free bill of quantities and programme of work so everyone knows what is expected.

  • Quoted from your drawings

    A free, no obligation quotation and full specification from your architect's drawings, plus a free programme of works with a start date and a finish date.

  • Billed as it is built

    With no up-front payment, completed work is billed monthly from the agreed bill of quantities.

  • Aftercare

    An after sale service, and a six-month retention held by larger clients.

The specification Woodlands Homes draws on

  • Underfloor heating
  • Pressurised hot water for high performance showers
  • Pilkington K glass for improved thermal values
  • Quality bathrooms
  • Purpose made windows and doors where required
  • Kitchens chosen to the customer's requirements
  • Staircases designed to suit the character of the project

Got land or a building plot?

Woodlands Homes is looking for building land and plots, with or without planning permission, including large gardens. Contact Dean for more information.
